page: Amazon Web Services r7a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. The system includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 instructions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA cryptography extensions. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

This instance configuration features no bundled local instance storage and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached storage for persistence. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. There are no discrete GPUs attached. In compute benchmarks, the processor demonstrates strong single-core capability, recording top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core tests (3075.89) and Geekbench single-core execution (1998.0). Multi-core throughput remains in the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core mark of 10348.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20038.21. In memory throughput tests, cached small-block reads achieve 1184.87 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached read bandwidth measures 38.35 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile.

The r7a.2xlarge architecture balances dedicated AMD core execution with high DDR5 memory density. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on external volumes for stateful data. With its 8:1 memory allocation and strong single-thread performance, the instance fits in-memory caching systems such as Redis, medium-scale transactional databases, real-time analytics, and data processing tasks requiring substantial RAM per core without requiring local disk caching.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro system, powered by an 8-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated physical cores and AVX-512 instruction support, it allocates 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and operates with a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded CPU capability, highlighted by high stress-ng and Geekbench single-core marks, alongside solid text processing performance. Multi-threaded compute, Redis throughput, and memory bandwidth sit within middle-tier ranges, with uncached large-block reads registering lower relative bandwidth. Given the high memory capacity per core and dedicated compute resources, the r7a.2xlarge is structured for memory-bound applications, including in-memory databases, Redis caches, data preprocessing pipelines, and relational database servers backed by network storage.
